GME: +~32% month to date; Ryan Cohen bought $26.4M (largest insider buy in company history) and $46.8M this month (~9% stake); 3 other directors bought; speculators positioning for an announcement. Reported, not recommended (453-505s)

Second-tier physical-infra names are still down: STRL -56% from its ~$1,000 peak, LGN halved from $107 (May), MOD halved. mustKnow.note: Ours' call omits the 7% and -62% numbers.

Closing view: nothing to own except AI (and occasionally bitcoin-related stocks) because the economy and markets are propped up by AI (1014-1080s)

ours.text: k5 and k9 both describe Burry's shorts (k9 says 'initiated', k5 says 'increased')
ours.problem: Duplicate, and 'initiated' is wrong: the transcript says 加码做空, meaning he added to existing shorts.

ours.text: k10: 'AI infrastructure shadow-banking and secondary physical infrastructure contractors (like STRL, LGN, and MOD) experienced steep valuation drawdowns of over 50% due to physical buildout bottlenecks'
ours.problem: Wrong causation and conflation. The creator attributes the drawdown to prior valuation overshoot, which overdrew years of earnings, followed by institutional profit-taking; bottlenecks explain why the narrative cannot be stretched further. Shadow banks (Apollo) are a separate point. LGN and MOD are 'halved', so 'over 50%' overstates slightly.

ours.text: k17: '...whereas secondary physical infrastructure contractors lack pricing power'
ours.problem: Pricing power is not mentioned; the transcript's contrast is about position in the chain (indirect beneficiaries) and valuation.

ours.text: k7: '...maintains upward pressure on bond yields'
ours.problem: An extrapolation: the creator only concludes that oil's downside is limited. Minor.
Misattribution: the SOXX short is Burry's position; the creator expresses no view and calls shorting MU 'very bold'.
False stance: TLT's decline is reported as market news, not a recommendation.

sentimentIssues: MU is entirely missing from tickerSentiment despite a Burry short, earnings on Sep 30 and consensus EPS $31.43 / NTM $144.94; the creator's stance (a short here is 'very bold') leans bullish or neutral on MU.
SOXX 'bearish/avoid' and TLT 'bearish/avoid' attribute third-party or market moves to the creator.
Resolution failures on obvious Latin tickers: spoken 'AMD' gets ticker null, and 'LGN' is null in one row and resolved in the other. Chinese names (麦当劳, 英伟达, 谷歌, 亚马逊, 阿波罗, 闪迪) are never mapped.
Duplicate rows: STRL x2 (avoid vs neutral), TLT x2 (avoid vs neutral), IONQ x2, LGN x2.
STRL/LGN/MOD bearish is correct; 'avoid' is defensible given the warning against averaging down, but stances differ across duplicate rows.
GME bullish/watch is right: reported, not recommended.
why: Ours covers nearly every segment (rates, auction, Bessent buyback, Citi/JPM, Iran/oil, GME, Burry, IONQ, Apollo, AI hardware split, RKT, MCD) with accurate numbers, and it keeps the one real call (RKT watch until cuts) correctly as a watch. LeapEdge misattributes Burry's short to 'Andrew MacKenzie', writes SMOD for MOD, invents a GME buy and an ES long trade, and misses IONQ, Apollo, Iran and the Bessent buyback. Ours' main weaknesses: MU earnings (Sep 30, EPS $31.43/$144.94) are omitted, the Burry item is duplicated, there are 19 keyPoints and 20 sentiment rows with many null tickers, and two stances wrongly attribute market or third-party moves to the creator.
recommendations: Add a Chinese-name ticker lexicon plus a Latin-token pass: 麦当劳->MCD, 英伟达->NVDA, 谷歌->GOOGL, 亚马逊->AMZN, 阿波罗->APO, 闪迪->SNDK, 英特(尔)->INTC, 美光->MU. Any spoken all-caps token such as 'AMD' or 'LGN' that matches a listed symbol must never be null.
Add a 'holder' field to sentiment rows (creator / third party / market). 'Burry 加码做空 SOXX' should read holder=Michael Burry, stance=short, not creator 'avoid'. 'TLT大跌' is a market move, not a stance.
Add an 'upcoming catalysts' block that always extracts dated events and consensus numbers: 'MU earnings Wed 9/30, FQ4 adj EPS est $31.43 (+940%), NTM EPS $144.94'. Ours dropped this entirely.
Cap keyPoints at ~8-10 and dedupe semantically (k5/k9 Burry, k15/k16 Apollo); rank by materiality. Nineteen points is not skimmable.
Make omissions truthful: generate them by diffing the transcript against the output, and drop items like 'Omitted IONQ...' when IONQ is in k14.

Do not add causal glue that the creator did not say: the STRL/LGN/MOD drawdown is 'valuation overdrew future earnings, plus institutional profit-taking', not 'due to physical buildout bottlenecks'. Add a critique check that flags 'due to/because' clauses without a transcript anchor.
Detect transcript gaps (this one skips 66-106s and 157-208s) and surface them, so users know that levels LeapEdge reports (S&P 7650/7800) may exist in audio we did not transcribe.
